nodes.label: Adaptive Personalization (Trader / Analyst / Casual modes)
nodes.rationale: Surface reshapes per user intent with deterministic narration, implementing PRODUCT.md's 'adapt to intent, stay one product' principle.

nodes.label: BTC Market Mood — multi-timeframe mood verdict product
nodes.rationale: Exists because reading multi-timeframe confluence on existing tools is either ugly-utilitarian (TradingView) or dumbed-down; success = trader trusts it at a glance and reaches for it over TradingView for a mood/confluence read.
nodes.norm_label: btc market mood — multi-timeframe mood verdict product

nodes.label: Primary Persona: Active Crypto Trader
nodes.rationale: Default persona the surface optimizes for first: reads mood across six timeframes in under a second, values speed/density/trust over hand-holding.

nodes.label: MyCryptoStack Design System (MDS) v0.3
nodes.rationale: Governing principle: specify, do not enumerate — every rule is an enforceable contract with a value/threshold so designers, devs, tooling and CI derive the same behavior without interpretation. Foundations defined mathematically before components so nothing is refactored later.

nodes.label: Three-Tier Token Architecture (Primitive → Semantic → Component)
nodes.rationale: Components never reference raw colors; theming swaps only the semantic layer, which is what makes the four themes maintainable.

nodes.label: Perceptual OKLCH Color (Obsidian Indigo direction)
nodes.rationale: OKLCH not hex for even lightness steps and clean gradients; never pure #000/#fff — neutrals tinted toward brand hue; APCA-scored contrast pairs required per release.

nodes.label: Elevation Recipe (surface steps + 1px specular hairline, e0–e3)
nodes.rationale: Depth on dark comes from surface-lightness steps + specular top hairline, not heavy shadows; the specular is 'the single biggest flat-to-crafted move'. Max 3 levels above canvas.
nodes.norm_label: elevation recipe (surface steps + 1px specular hairline, e0–e3)

nodes.label: Numeral Design Language (B5): tabular mono, decimal alignment, precision rules
nodes.rationale: Numbers are most of a trading UI so they get their own contract: Geist Mono tabular-nums, precision as max(exchange tick, magnitude), locale-aware (USD + INR lakh/crore), ≤250ms tick-flash on change.
nodes.norm_label: numeral design language (b5): tabular mono, decimal alignment, precision rules

nodes.label: Motion Grammar (ease-out only, 120–300ms, transform/opacity only)
nodes.rationale: No bounce/elastic; layout-affecting properties forbidden (lift via translateY, not top); every animation carries a prefers-reduced-motion fallback.

nodes.label: Component Platform (C): Panel, Num, DataTable and primitives with full contracts
nodes.rationale: Built only after Foundations (B) is frozen; every component documents the same contract (anatomy, tokens, states, a11y, keyboard, responsive, anti-patterns) and consumes component-tier tokens only.
nodes.norm_label: component platform (c): panel, num, datatable and primitives with full contracts

nodes.label: C-FREEZE: Panel primitive frozen 2026-06-27
nodes.rationale: No new local panel/card/widget implementations in pages; new behavior extends the shared Panel via props and re-runs the Visual Regression Checklist rather than forking a variant. Enforced by eslint no-restricted-syntax in CI.

nodes.label: B5-FREEZE: Num component is the only legal financial-value renderer
nodes.rationale: Callers choose a SEMANTIC variant (Num.Price/Money/Pnl/Pct/Delta/RR/Qty/Score/Compact), never raw formatting; no toLocaleString/toFixed in pages — new value types add a variant in Num.tsx.
nodes.norm_label: b5-freeze: num component is the only legal financial-value renderer

nodes.label: H-FREEZE: DataTable Column<T> API frozen at v1.0
nodes.rationale: Validated across all four table archetypes (Analytics, Comparison, Historical, Diagnostic) with no API change, so frozen. Fixed layering: DataTable → Column Presets → Financial Cells → Num.*; v2 features are additive, never a fork.
nodes.norm_label: h-freeze: datatable column<t> api frozen at v1.0

nodes.label: Financial Data Visualization Grammar (D): chart-type matrix, color budget, overlay z-order
nodes.rationale: Chart type chosen by intent, never novelty; ≤6 distinct hues per chart; fixed 7-layer overlay stacking order with crosshair/tooltip always on top.
nodes.norm_label: financial data visualization grammar (d): chart-type matrix, color budget, overlay z-order

nodes.label: Explainable AI Grammar (E): never a score without its reasons
nodes.rationale: The differentiator. 11 required AI-card slots (verdict, confidence, direction, evidence, counter-signals, risk, history, source, uncertainty, action, affordances); contradictory evidence surfaced, never hidden; empty slots render honest empty states, never fabricated values.
nodes.norm_label: explainable ai grammar (e): never a score without its reasons

nodes.label: Market State Grammar (F): orthogonal perceptual channels per dimension
nodes.rationale: Direction, confidence, risk, volatility, liquidity and signal-agreement each own an independent visual channel; green must not mean both 'up' and 'confident'. Conflicting signals are a first-class state rendered side-by-side, never averaged into one number.
nodes.norm_label: market state grammar (f): orthogonal perceptual channels per dimension

nodes.label: Dashboard Grammar & Cognitive Load Budget (G): viewport/color/motion/alert budgets + IHS ≥ 80
nodes.rationale: Measurable limits so dashboards stay usable as features are added; widget cap is a function of density mode (resolves the old 4-vs-8 contradiction); accent+semantic pixel coverage ≤10%, gold ≤2%.
nodes.norm_label: dashboard grammar & cognitive load budget (g): viewport/color/motion/alert budgets + ihs ≥ 80

nodes.label: Financial Tables Contract (H): alignment, sticky, sort, virtualization >100 rows
nodes.rationale: Numbers never truncate (reduce density or wrap the column instead); live-updated rows never reflow or jump — they animate position only when the active sort demands it.
nodes.norm_label: financial tables contract (h): alignment, sticky, sort, virtualization >100 rows

nodes.label: State Transition Grammar (I): Loading→Ready→Live→Stale→Disconnected lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Never render stale data as if live; never blank the screen on disconnect (freeze last value and label it); AI/confidence cards downgrade when their inputs are stale.

nodes.label: Responsive Trading Layouts (J): panel is the responsive unit, ultrawide adds panels
nodes.rationale: Trading needs more than phone breakpoints — 7 environments up to multi-monitor floating windows; extra width adds workspace columns, never stretches one panel; line length ≤75ch.
nodes.norm_label: responsive trading layouts (j): panel is the responsive unit, ultrawide adds panels

nodes.label: Plugin & Extension Architecture (K): CustomIndicator, AIProvider, ExchangeConnector contracts
nodes.rationale: Extension points are versioned, capability-scoped, sandboxed contracts from day one; an AIProvider that cannot supply evidence + confidence is rejected; contracts bind to existing code (lib/indicatorFramework, golden-master harness, lib/dataSource registry).
nodes.norm_label: plugin & extension architecture (k): customindicator, aiprovider, exchangeconnector contracts

nodes.label: Engineering Platform (L): frozen-contract lint, token lint, 250KB bundle budget, Storybook, axe
nodes.rationale: Transforms the design system from a document into an enforceable standard — freezes are enforced by lint in CI, not code review; single-source theming via one [data-theme] block per theme in app/globals.css.
nodes.norm_label: engineering platform (l): frozen-contract lint, token lint, 250kb bundle budget, storybook, axe

nodes.label: Indicator Strategy: bucket, don't transpile
nodes.rationale: No PineScript transpiler or JS Pine runtime (weeks of work, correctness risk, most indicators aren't custom Pine). Bucket A = indicatorts library wiring (~10 min each); Bucket B = hand-port golden-master gated; Bucket C = already built. Library-backed does NOT mean TradingView-identical — golden master catches divergence (VWAP anchoring, Keltner basis, Stochastic smoothing).

nodes.label: Multi-Indicator Stack Engine (1B): activeIndicatorIds[], namespaced instanceKey::plotId
nodes.rationale: Lifts the structural limit of exactly one active indicator; series namespaced instanceKey::plotId fixes Bollinger/Keltner basis collisions; oscillator panes rebuilt only on signature change (per-tick just pushes data) to survive pane-index shifts; stack persists to localStorage and share URL (?ind=, URL wins).
nodes.norm_label: multi-indicator stack engine (1b): activeindicatorids[], namespaced instancekey::plotid

nodes.label: Decoupled SVG Drawing Layer (7 tools, per-symbol persistence)
nodes.rationale: Built as a decoupled SVG overlay over the chart rather than threading state through the chart's fragile canvas pointer machine; drawings positioned in chart-time/price space so they stick on pan/zoom; keyed by symbol in localStorage.
nodes.norm_label: decoupled svg drawing layer (7 tools, per-symbol persistence)

nodes.label: MTF Confluence Ribbon (time-aligned per-TF signal heatmap)
nodes.rationale: The differentiator TradingView structurally lacks: one row per timeframe, each a time-aligned heatmap over the selected chart window; colorblind-safe (color + glyph + label); click a row to switch TF.
nodes.norm_label: mtf confluence ribbon (time-aligned per-tf signal heatmap)

nodes.label: Timeframe-Group Divergence Callouts (lower 1m–15m vs higher 1h–1d bias)
nodes.norm_label: timeframe-group divergence callouts (lower 1m–15m vs higher 1h–1d bias)

nodes.label: Chart→Trade One Surface (right-click orders, draggable TP/SL updates position)
nodes.norm_label: chart→trade one surface (right-click orders, draggable tp/sl updates position)

nodes.label: Bar Replay (cut-point selector, scrub, speeds, bookmarks, isolated session)
nodes.rationale: Replay state slices the candle array to the play index so indicators replay too; exits on TF/symbol change.
nodes.norm_label: bar replay (cut-point selector, scrub, speeds, bookmarks, isolated session)

nodes.label: Price Alerts (model + reactive store, dashed price lines, cross-fire notification)
nodes.norm_label: price alerts (model + reactive store, dashed price lines, cross-fire notification)

nodes.label: Renko Box-Size Methods (Traditional / ATR / Percentage)
nodes.rationale: Chart types deliberately limited to Candlestick/Heikin-Ashi/Renko — Line/Area/Baseline/Bars/Hollow intentionally not wanted because they'd require re-attaching order-overlay/FX/marker primitives bound to the candle series.

nodes.label: Porting PineScript Indicators to TypeScript (guide)
nodes.rationale: Hand-porting Pine into native TS is right for a curated, fast, auditable first-party library — but a port that looks right can still disagree with TradingView by enough to flip a signal, and silent divergence is the worst failure mode for a trading tool. Hence: every ported indicator ships with a golden-master test, no exceptions.

nodes.label: Golden-Master Test Harness (lib/testing/goldenMaster.ts)
nodes.rationale: A fixture pins fixed candles + params to expected plot values and signals; test recomputes and compares within tolerance (abs 1e-6, rel 1e-4). Never blindly refresh a failing golden test — that defeats the entire point.

nodes.label: Fixture Provenance: tradingview (correctness) vs snapshot (regression-only)
nodes.rationale: A snapshot baseline catches drift but cannot prove the original port was right; upgrade to a tradingview-sourced fixture as soon as real candle data can be captured.

nodes.label: PineScript Port Pitfalls Checklist (RMA vs EMA, population stdev, na warm-up, var persistence)
nodes.rationale: The Pine semantics an LLM or human most often gets subtly wrong: ta.rsi/atr/adx use Wilder's RMA not SMA/EMA (the #1 silent bug); ta.stdev is population (divides by N); warm-up off-by-one shifts every value; needing a looser tolerance is a smell, widen only with written justification.
nodes.norm_label: pinescript port pitfalls checklist (rma vs ema, population stdev, na warm-up, var persistence)

nodes.label: TradingView Fixture Workflow (CSV export → golden fixture)
nodes.norm_label: tradingview fixture workflow (csv export → golden fixture)

nodes.label: TradingView RSI PineScript v6 source (RMA-based, smoothing MA, divergence pivots)
nodes.rationale: Original Pine source kept in-repo so the TS port is auditable against its origin, per the porting conventions.
nodes.norm_label: tradingview rsi pinescript v6 source (rma-based, smoothing ma, divergence pivots)

nodes.label: Chart Smoke Test (manual browser checklist, ~10 min, 14 sections)
nodes.rationale: Exists because chart-rendering components (Chart.tsx, DrawingLayer.tsx, panes, overlays) have no automated coverage — tsc/vitest/next build pass but rendering and interaction are only verifiable in a browser.
nodes.norm_label: chart smoke test (manual browser checklist, ~10 min, 14 sections)

nodes.label: TradingView-grade Layout Redesign Checklist (fixed instrument frame)
nodes.rationale: Move from a vertical-stack dashboard to a TV-style fixed frame: chart fills the stage, everything else docks or floats, zero scroll to see the chart; the chart must never jump.
nodes.norm_label: tradingview-grade layout redesign checklist (fixed instrument frame)

nodes.label: BottomDock (collapsible tabbed bottom panel: Trades/Stats/Backtest/Alerts/Indicators)
nodes.rationale: Highest-leverage move: always-rendered stacked page sections migrate into one drag-resizable, collapsible dock so the chart reclaims the viewport.

nodes.label: Fixed Non-Relayouting Frame (Header → toolbar | chart | dock fills viewport)
nodes.norm_label: fixed non-relayouting frame (header → toolbar | chart | dock fills viewport)

nodes.label: Timeframe Quick-Row in Toolbar (inline 15m/1h/4h/1D + overflow dropdown)
nodes.norm_label: timeframe quick-row in toolbar (inline 15m/1h/4h/1d + overflow dropdown)

nodes.label: Playwright CT Harness — Chart smoke tests entry HTML
nodes.norm_label: playwright ct harness — chart smoke tests entry html
